home_intro: is the OCI application package format for Linux desktops, servers and devices.
home_store_intro: Every package has a clear manifest, a real origin and a command you can inspect before installing it.
home_learn_title: Learn cpak by making it decide
home_learn_intro: Follow a complete course, change real manifests and see what cpak accepts, refuses or changes. Professional paths lead to an exam and a public, verifiable credential.
home_everywhere_intro: Works out of the box on every Linux distribution.
feature_footprint_desc: Two static binaries provide the runtime and one shared content store for every application.
feature_docker_desc: Familiar Dockerfile syntax, layer caching and incremental builds without a container daemon in production.
feature_nvidia_desc: Bind host graphics drivers at launch instead of packaging a second driver stack in every image.
feature_secure_desc: Declare access to DBus, sockets and devices. Grant only the resources an application needs.
feature_git_desc: Install any tag, branch or exact commit SHA, then pin the source that should receive updates.
feature_build_desc: Use the same manifest and command across systems, with an OCI image built for each architecture.
docs_title: Everything you need to build and ship with cpak.
docs_intro: Choose the path that matches what you are doing. Each guide uses the current v2 runtime, manifest and command line interface.
docs_use_desc: Install the runtime, check your host and run an application.
docs_package_desc: Turn an OCI image and a small manifest into a distributable application.
docs_work_desc: Understand the repository map, development flow and project conventions.
docs_missing_desc: The documentation is maintained beside the project. Open the repository, inspect the code or propose a focused correction.
announcements_intro: Notes on new packages, runtime changes and the projects that choose to ship with cpak.
store_intro: Find {count} desktop applications, development tools and complete environments packaged for cpak.
learn_title: Learn how cpak works by making it decide.
learn_intro: Follow a course, edit real manifests and see what cpak accepts, refuses or changes. Read everything without an account, then sign in when you want progress across machines or a credential.
courses_intro: Each path has its own curriculum and closing quiz. The professional paths continue into an exam.
credentials_intro: Course quizzes stay in the course. Role exams are marked on the server and issue a signed credential with a public verification page.
workspaces_title: Use cpak before touching your machine
workspaces_intro: Write the input you would use on Linux and read the validation, policy or migration result.
footer_description: Decentralized software distribution for any context.
all_lessons_done: Every lesson is marked done. The closing questions are where you check what you understood.
browser_progress_note: Progress is kept in this browser. An account keeps it across machines, and every lesson remains available without one.
exam_course_intro: The course quiz checks your understanding. Pass this exam to receive a credential under your account with a public verification page.
exam_attempt_intro: {questions} questions. {pass} per cent to pass. You may take it again as many times as you like, and a later pass replaces an earlier one.
exam_context: Open book, taken on your own machine, with nobody watching. The credential records an exam result under an account and nothing more.
exam_server_marking: Answers are marked on the server. The page never receives the answer key and a failed sitting is not recorded.
credential_issued: A credential has been issued under your account with a public verification page.
exam_failed_help: {pass} per cent is required. Review the course and try again. The questions you missed are not shown because the next sitting uses the same exam.
keep_sitting_intro: Your answers stay in this browser while you work. Finish the exam, then create an account to submit it and receive a credential.
finish_remaining_one: Finish the last question to submit the exam.
finish_remaining_many: Finish the {remaining} remaining questions to submit the exam.
answers_saved: Your answers are saved in this browser.
create_account_submit: Create an account to submit them.
quiz_intro: {questions} questions on what you just read. Nothing is saved or issued. Use the result to see which of the {lessons} lessons to revisit while they are still open in the rail.
quiz_intro_playground: One question uses the playground on this page.
quiz_perfect: All correct. You can now read a manifest and tell what the application can do.
quiz_one_wrong: Review one answer. Its explanation points to the lesson.
quiz_retry_help: Read the explanations above, then reopen the relevant lessons from the rail.
policy_workspace_intro: Write every side of the decision and read the policy that reaches the container.
policy_effective_intro: The manifest or saved local override asks. A managed ceiling can only remove access.
desktop_workspace_intro: Edit the file shipped by the image and the export request cpak receives.
desktop_example_near_misses: Lines that only look like Exec
desktop_example_no_group: A file with no [Desktop Entry] group
filesystem_workspace_intro: Write the manifest list and the host it will be resolved against.
filesystem_example_editor: What a text editor asks for
filesystem_example_player: What a media player asks for
filesystem_mount_plan_intro: Every accepted line shows its host source and path inside the application.
migration_workspace_intro: Paste a complete manifest and read the version 2 file cpak would write.
permissions_workspace_intro: Edit the manifest, then read the validation result.
permissions_host_summary: one desktop user on a Wayland session, uid 1000, home /home/ada
permissions_available: Permission names available in this build
permissions_available_intro: Add a key under override and the result above changes immediately.
permission_socket_at_spi_bus: Mount the AT-SPI accessibility bus socket
permission_device_serial: Expose USB and CDC serial ports
permission_host_applications: Expose and launch desktop applications from the host
permission_as_root: Run as root inside the container
credential_superseded_line: Superseded by a later result for the same exam.
credential_local_account: Local development account {handle}, not checked against any provider
credential_claim: This is the result of an open-book online exam. The account named above was authenticated; the candidate's identity and exam session were not supervised.
credential_immutable: Each result is permanent. A later pass supersedes it, and its current status ends on the expiry date.
credential_later_result: The later result was issued on {date}.
credential_replaced_at: The result that replaced it is at
certificate_note: The signed credential record remains the source of truth.
certificate_intro: A printable copy of the result, connected to the signed public record by its credential code.
certificate_passed: has passed the open-book role exam
verify_record_intro: This is the complete record, including the limits of what it certifies.
verify_for_someone: If you are checking this on someone's behalf
verify_for_someone_text: The account named above passed this exam on the recorded date. The exam was open book and unsupervised, so this record does not identify who was at the keyboard.
verify_material_text: The exam and its course are public. You can inspect what the credential covers in
verify_missing_intro: No record matches {code}. Check the code you received. It contains sixteen case-insensitive characters in four groups.
verify_missing_reuse: Codes are never reused, so this result will not change later.
verify_lookup_intro: Paste a credential code or verification address to read the complete public record.
verify_code_help: Case does not matter, and the dashes are optional.
verify_record_says_text: It says that the named account passed the exam on the recorded date. The exam is open book and unsupervised, so it does not identify the person at the keyboard or what they consulted.
verify_record_permanent: A record is permanent. A later pass supersedes it, and its current status ends on the expiry date, while the original result remains readable.
verify_code_only: A code is the only way in
verify_code_only_text: Records cannot be searched by name. The holder must share the credential code or its verification address. Requests are rate limited.
account_erased_summary: Removed {completions} completed lesson records, {sessions} sessions and {accounts} account records from the server. This browser was cleared and signed out.
account_erased_credentials: {count} public credential records remain available at their verification addresses. Sign in with the same account to list them again.
account_memory_server: This development server stores accounts in memory.
account_no_database: No database is bound to this deployment. Accounts, progress and credentials exist only in server memory and disappear when it restarts.
account_browser_intro: Completed lessons are saved in this browser. Sign in to sync them across machines.
account_nothing_yet: Nothing yet. Complete a lesson to see it here.
account_signin_intro: Lessons and playgrounds work without an account. Sign in to sync progress and sit an exam that issues a credential.
account_github_public: GitHub provides the public handle recorded on a credential.
account_github_scope: cpak reads your handle, numeric id and avatar. It cannot modify your GitHub account.
account_local_warning: Local sign-in is available only during development and does not verify the handle. Credentials issued here are marked as local.
account_signin_unavailable: Sign-in is not configured on this deployment. Courses and playgrounds remain available.
account_worked_intro: Lessons you marked complete, synced with this account.
account_start_anywhere: Nothing yet. Start anywhere in cpak Learn and completed lessons appear here.
account_badges_intro: Finishing every lesson earns a private course badge. Public credentials come from the role exams below.
account_badges_none: None yet. Finish every lesson in a course to earn its badge.
account_credentials_intro: Credentials record an exam result under this account and have a public verification page.
account_credentials_none: None yet. Passing an exam while signed in adds one here.
account_exams_repeat: They are open book and can be repeated.
account_data_identity: Your {provider} handle, numeric account id and avatar address. No email address is requested or stored.
account_data_progress: One record for each lesson you marked complete, including its title and completion date.
account_data_sessions: One record for each open session, storing a hash of its cookie. Sessions expire after thirty days.
account_data_credentials: One permanent record for each issued credential.
account_data_visibility: Course progress and sessions are private. Credentials are public at their verification addresses. The pages you read are not recorded.
account_delete_intro: Remove the account, completed lessons and open sessions from the server and this browser, then sign out.
account_delete_credentials: This does not remove your {count} public credential records. Signing in again with the same account lists them here again.
credential_page_intro: Share its verification link or download a certificate for your records.
credential_public_intro: This address is public and names your {handleType}. Share it with whoever needs to verify the result.
credential_copy_failed: This browser could not write to the clipboard. Select and copy the address.
credential_not_deletable_intro: Deleting account data removes progress and open sessions, but this public credential remains available. Signing in again with the same account lists it again.
